To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the G1 cells of excised pea root meristem are induced to progress through the S and G2 periods by relatively short intervals of sucrose spurt and that the duration of the S and G, stages is dependent on the duration of the sucrose spurt.
cells can be induced to progress through the cell cycle in the absence of cell division and that the cell cycle is regulated by carbohydrate provision.
the mitotic cycle of plant cells can be manipulated by the provision of exogenous sucrose and that the S and G2 stages are more sensitive to sucrose than the G1 and G4 stages.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the control of cell proliferation in the meristematic region of the root tip of Pisum sativum by carbohydrate availability.
the role of carbohydrates in the control of the progression of cells through the mitotic cycle.
the role of carbohydrate availability in the control of cell division in plant roots.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the G1 cells of excised roots can be induced to enter the cell cycle by short intervals of carbohydrate availability.
the mitotic cycle of the root meristem cell is controlled through the G1 stage, which appears to have a relatively greater dependence on carbohydrate availability.

cells of excised pea root meristem are arrested in a stationary phase by prolonged carbohydrate deprivation and can be induced to enter the mitotic cycle by relatively short periods of carbohydrate provision.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cells in G1 can be positioned and retained at any stage of the mitotic cell cycle by varying the duration and/or frequency of carbohydrate provision.
the mitotic cycle can be manipulated to some extent by the provision or deprivation of carbohydrates.

the G1 cells in the stationary phase of the root meristem were arrested in the cycle by a deficiency in carbohydrate availability and were induced to enter S when provided a short interval of carbohydrate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mitotic cycle is a flexible process that is responsive to changes in the carbohydrate environment.
the mitotic cycle is a dynamic process that is responsive to environmental signals.
cells in the stationary phase can be manipulated into the S period of the cycle and retained there.
